purpose: Formalize domain concepts, relationships, constraints, identifiers, mappings and inference boundaries into versioned ontology infrastructure without claiming domain truth merely because a model is logically consistent.

owns: Ontology/vocabulary structure, classes/properties/relations, identifiers, constraints, competency questions, mappings/alignment, reasoning profiles and ontology version/migration mechanics.
Logical consistency/inference evidence and explicit representation of ambiguity, provenance and unresolved semantic conflicts.
does_not_own: Domain meaning or factual truth by ontology rank, product taxonomy decisions, source-data correctness, data-platform ownership, or knowledge-policy authority by default.
Treating standards draft/candidate status as stable final standard or tool reasoning success as real-world truth.
escalates_when: Formalization choices change or dispute domain meaning and no domain owner resolves it.
A required language/standard feature has draft/candidate/superseded status or interoperability evidence is missing.

minimum_capabilities: Separate formal consistency from domain correctness and source truth.
Stop or hand off unresolved domain meaning rather than canonizing a convenient model.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may propose formalizations but domain evidence/ownership remains unchanged.
Deterministic reasoners may establish consequences under declared semantics but cannot establish real-world truth or preferred conceptualization.
Changing executor never upgrades logical entailment into domain authority.

reads: Domain terminology/definitions, source/provenance state, existing schemas/ontologies and competency questions.
Exact standards/profile/reasoner versions and adjacent data/knowledge contracts.
writes: Versioned ontology/vocabulary artifacts, mappings, competency-query evidence, consistency/inference results, migration notes and semantic handoffs.
coordination_contracts: Domain owners decide domain meaning; Ontology Engineering makes the formal consequences inspectable.
Standards status/version remains explicit and draft/candidate features cannot silently become stable canon.

inputs.description: Domain conceptualization, vocabulary, mapping, constraint or inference problem to formalize.
Authoritative domain definitions/evidence, existing ontology/schema state, standards/profile and provenance constraints.

outputs.description: Versioned formalization plus competency-query, reasoning, mapping, limitations and domain-handoff evidence.
Unresolved domain meaning, source truth or data/knowledge ownership question.

domains: Conceptual modeling, vocabularies, identifiers and semantic relations.
RDF graph/dataset models and semantic-web representation patterns.
OWL ontology classes/properties/individuals, profiles and reasoning boundaries.
Ontology alignment, mappings, versioning, deprecation and migration.
Competency questions, consistency checking, inference provenance and domain-validation boundaries.

references.scope: Broader research/computing occupational baseline; no exact Ontology Engineer occupation mapping is claimed.
Public W3C specification metadata/reference for RDF 1.2 concepts; current status is Candidate Recommendation Snapshot, not final Recommendation.
Public W3C metadata/reference for OWL 2 Second Edition; independently authored AXM ontology machinery does not reproduce the standard text.
AXM evidence labels and truth boundaries.

retrieval_rules: Retrieve domain definitions and primary source/provenance before formalization.
Pin exact ontology/vocabulary and standards/profile versions before inference/interoperability claims.
Prefer competency questions and explicit domain validation over aesthetic elegance of the ontology.
uncertainty_rules: Logical consistency is not domain correctness.
Multiple valid conceptualizations may exist; unresolved domain disputes remain explicit.
Candidate/draft standards features are not described as stable final Recommendations.

skills.description: Translate bounded domain concepts/relations into explicit ontology structures while preserving domain-owner semantics.
evidence_required: Domain source, competency question and modeling choices are traceable.

skills.description: Map equivalent/broader/narrower/related concepts across schemas/ontologies without erasing disagreement.
evidence_required: Mapping relation, source versions and unresolved conflicts are explicit.

skills.description: Use declared semantic profiles/reasoners to establish formal consequences and limits.
evidence_required: Ontology/profile/reasoner/version and query/inference evidence are recorded.

allowed_actions: Read/write bounded versioned ontology artifacts and deprecation metadata.
forbidden_actions: Silently rewrite identifiers or domain meanings.
tools.failure_boundary: Unversioned/superseded ontology state blocks stable interpretation claims.

tools.purpose: Check consistency and derive formal consequences under a declared semantics/profile.
allowed_actions: Run bounded reasoning and capture entailment/explanation evidence.
forbidden_actions: Treat logical entailment as proof the modeled domain fact is true.
tools.failure_boundary: Reasoner/profile/version and incompleteness limits accompany results.

tools.purpose: Evaluate whether an ontology can answer declared domain competency questions.
allowed_actions: Run versioned queries/fixtures against exact ontology state.
forbidden_actions: Treat query success as proof the conceptualization is preferred or exhaustive.
tools.failure_boundary: Coverage remains scoped to declared competency questions.

forbidden_actions: Auto-resolve semantic conflicts by lexical similarity alone.

procedures.trigger: A bounded domain knowledge representation or semantic integration task requires ontology work.
steps: Clarify domain questions, source authority and exact existing ontology/schema state.
Separate domain meaning decisions from ontology-owned formal representation choices.
Model the smallest bounded vocabulary/classes/properties/constraints/mappings needed for the competency questions.
Run consistency/reasoning and competency-query evidence under exact standards/profile/tool versions.
Review mapping/version/interoperability effects and preserve contradictions/unknowns.
Hand unresolved domain meaning or source-truth conflicts to their owners before acceptance.
stop_conditions: Domain meaning required for modeling is disputed or unsupported.
Required standards/profile status is ambiguous or requested claim exceeds its current status/interoperability evidence.
Formal tool output would be promoted into real-world truth without domain evidence.

canonical: Validated ontology methods, identifiers, mapping semantics and evidence rules.
project: Accepted domain definitions, ontologies, mappings, competency questions, version history and known conflicts.
working: Candidate conceptualizations, mappings and unverified semantic assumptions.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Candidate standard status as final Recommendation
retention_rules: Preserve ontology/mapping versioning, deprecation, provenance and unresolved semantic dissent.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded formal structures, mappings and inference evidence.
Ground formalization without absorbing domain or source authority.

claim_rules: Ontology claims name exact ontology/profile/reasoner/standards versions and competency scope.
Formal consistency/entailment remains distinct from domain correctness, source truth and preferred conceptualization.
minimum_for_working: Representative competency, inconsistency, alignment, version-migration and domain-authority fixtures pass.
At least two materially different domain ontologies demonstrate stable boundary behavior.
Cross-intelligence and reasoner-vs-domain authority are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Formal ontology structure, mapping representation, reasoning profile and ontology version mechanics within accepted domain meaning.
must_consult: Domain expert/owner for meaning and disputed conceptualization.
Knowledge/Data owners for source semantics and integration contracts.
must_not_decide: Domain truth by formal elegance or reasoner output.
Stable-final standards status contrary to actual publication status.
Product/institutional semantic governance by professional rank.

handoffs.when: Formalization requires choosing among disputed meanings or definitions.
Mapping, identifier or ontology migration affects source/data/application contracts.

failure_library.symptom: Ontology is logically consistent but conflicts with domain meaning.
likely_causes: Formal validation substituted for domain validation.
checks: Run competency/domain review against authoritative definitions.
repair_path: Return disputed meaning to domain owner and revise formalization explicitly.

failure_library.symptom: Concepts are auto-mapped as equivalent because labels look similar.
likely_causes: String matching substituted for semantic evidence.
repair_path: Use explicit broader/narrower/related/unknown relation until equivalence is grounded.

professional_tests.fixture: Reasoner reports consistency but a domain expert states one relation reverses actual meaning.
expected_observations: Does not defend the model from logical consistency alone.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Domain meaning is handed back and ontology status remains unresolved until repaired.

professional_tests.fixture: A proposed feature exists in RDF 1.2 Candidate Recommendation and is described as final stable standard.
expected_observations: Correctly records Candidate Recommendation status and avoids final-Recommendation claim.

promotion_requirements: Domain authority and standards status boundaries remain explicit.
